newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rises for first time in five sessions.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rises for first time in five sessions.

text.p: The Czech PX50 posted its first gain in five sessions on Wednesday led by moderate rises for the four most heavily capitalised shares.
The PX50 closed up 0.2 percent to 495.1 with turnover relatively high at 1.5 billion crowns.
The blue chip resurgence was led by SPT Telecom which rose 45 crowns to 3,400 and Komercni Banka moved up 10 crowns to 1,740.
Losses to SPT earlier in the week had been widely attributed by dealers to profit taking after strong gains last week.

Komercni Banka's run of losses has been put down to more fundamental factors especially the high interest rate regime of the Czech central bank which analysts say has raised the prospect of increased bad debt problems this year.

"Added to this general increase in asset risk, we are concerned at the prospect of the bank reporting significant unrealised bond losses from the slump in bond values in late May," ING Barings said in a report to investors.
"We have downgraded Komercni from a long term buy to a hold at the current prices," it added.
